name: Semiconductor fab
bpBasis: The 2 BP #72 gives for a chip fab, from the design sketch, whose two semiconductor fabs this building follows: 2.5 t of electronic silicon a month at 60 MW, or 1.2 t of radiation-hardened ICs a month at 80 MW

name: Solar cell fab
bpBasis: Sized by silicon cells at 1 t an hour, 8,760 t a year, about 4.0 GW a year at the 2.2 g of silicon a watt Fraunhofer ISE gives for 2022 (silicon used, sawing losses included); Mission Solar is building 2 GW a year of cells in Texas for $265M (2025), scaled linearly to $527M

name: Battery plant
bpBasis: Sized by lithium-ion cells at 1 t an hour, 8,760 t a year, 2.1 GWh a year at the 243 Wh/kg of the Panasonic NCR18650B cell; Benchmark Mineral Intelligence gives over $100M a GWh of new cell capacity in North America (2023), so $213M

name: Magnet works
bpBasis: Sized by sintered NdFeB magnets at 1 t an hour, 8,760 t a year; Neo Performance Materials built 2,000 t a year in Narva, Estonia, for $75M (2025), scaled linearly to $329M

name: Data centre
bpBasis: The 1.8 BP #72 gives for a 120 MW data centre, the size of this one, $15M a MW; the Cushman & Wakefield 2026 Data Center Development Cost Guide gives $17.6M a MW all-in for a greenfield site in the United States and Canada, excluding chips and GPUs
